title: Complications and Their Risk Factors in Orthognathic Surgery: A Retrospective Single-Center Study
summary:
Orthognathic surgery is a procedure used to correct problems with the position of the jaws and facial bones. Its goal is to improve how the teeth fit together, enhance facial appearance, and support important functions such as chewing, breathing, and jaw movement.
The surgery involves cutting and repositioning the jaw bones into a more natural and correct position. It is a well-established and generally safe procedure, but complications can sometimes occur after surgery, such as reduced sensation in the lips or chin, jaw joint problems, relapse of the correction, or infections.
Although studies on these complications exist, many include only small numbers of patients. Also, the relationship between surgery-related factors and the risk of complications has not been widely studied in large patient groups.

interventions.name:
All surgical cases of orthognathic osteotomies performed between 2019 and 2024 will be recorded and analyzed.
There are approximately 500 cases in our records.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The following inclusion criteria were used:
patients older than 18 years old, at the end of growth, who accepted the informed consent
patients suffering of malocclusion or OSAS
no history of maxillofacial trauma
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria were used:
syndromic patients, since they are statistically more prone to complications (Zaroni et al., 2024)
